about.title: Davis Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Davis recorded 200 injury collisions and one traffic death in the most recent final crash year, numbers that represent real families along corridors like I-80, 5th Street, Russell Boulevard, and Mace Boulevard. When a collision takes a loved one, the grief is immediate, but California law also puts a clock on legal action. Surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children have priority standing to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents or heirs eligible in other circumstances. These claims are separate from any criminal charges that may follow a fatal crash and focus instead on the financial and emotional losses left behind. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect grieving families in Davis with an independent attorney who can explain standing, deadlines, and what losses may be recoverable. There's no cost to start the conversation, and no fee unless the case results in a recovery.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific people, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children. An independent attorney can help clarify where your family fits before pursuing a claim.

items.title: A Firm Two-Year Deadline
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity require faster action. Missing that window can close the door on recovery entirely.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral costs and lost financial support, along with compensation for lost love, companionship, and guidance. An attorney can help document these losses accurately.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Davis?
items.answer: California generally sets a two-year deadline from the date of death for wrongful death claims. If the crash involved a government-owned road or vehicle, a much shorter deadline may apply, so it's worth getting guidance early. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who can confirm the timeline for your situation.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim after a Davis crash?
items.answer: California law gives first priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing under certain circumstances. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and explain where you stand.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim relate to Davis crash corridors like I-80 or Mace Boulevard?
items.answer: Public crash records show collision activity along corridors including I-80, 5th Street, Russell Boulevard, and Mace Boulevard, with Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. seeing frequent reports. These are simply public-record patterns, not a judgment about any specific road. If a loved one was lost in a crash on one of these routes, an attorney can look into the details of what happened.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensating the family, regardless of whether criminal charges are filed against the at-fault driver. The two processes run independently and can proceed on different timelines.
